draft.title: Mining and internal migration
card: Mining is the digging up of minerals and fuels, such as iron ore and coal. A mining boom is a time when demand and prices are high, so mines expand and need many workers.

Mines are often in remote regions, such as the Pilbara in Western Australia (iron ore) and the Bowen Basin in Queensland (coal). These regions have few people living in them, so workers must come from elsewhere.
Some workers move to a nearby town to live. This is internal migration, because they stay inside Australia.
Others work fly-in fly-out (FIFO). They live in a city such as Perth or Brisbane, fly to the mine for a roster of days, then fly home for time off.
draft.remember: Mining booms pull workers to remote regions, and FIFO workers do the job without living there.

a.q: Why do mining booms lead to internal migration to regions such as the Pilbara?
opts: Mines need many workers, and few people live nearby
Mines are built close to the large capital cities
Workers from other countries are not allowed to come
Mining jobs are the only jobs in Australia's regions
a.why: Mines are in remote regions with few residents, so a boom draws workers from other parts of Australia. Mines are not built near the capital cities, which is why workers have to travel.
a.clue: Think about who already lives in a remote region.

b.q: Tom lives in Adelaide with his family. He works two weeks at a coal mine in the Bowen Basin, flies home for one week, then repeats. Which describes his work?
opts: Fly-in fly-out work, as he lives away from the mine
Permanent migration, as he has moved to the mine
International migration, as he crosses state borders
Forced migration, as his job makes him travel
b.why: Tom lives in Adelaide and flies to the mine for a roster, so he is a FIFO worker. He has not moved to the mine region to live there, so it is not a permanent move. Travelling between states is still within Australia, so it is not international.
b.clue: Where does Tom live when he is not at work?

a.best: Mines need many workers, and few people live nearby

b.best: Fly-in fly-out work, as he lives away from the mine

problems.detail: Why (a) says 'Mines are not built near the capital cities', an absolute claim. The card only says mines are 'often' in remote regions, and some mines and quarries do operate near cities. It should say mines are often far from the capitals.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer, and the card's facts check out. Why (a) overstates the card by saying mines are not built near capital cities, when the card says they are 'often' remote.
